# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 3 | **Condition:** Fragmentary

---

**3:1** [...] I give thanks to You, O Lord, for You have made my face to shine for Your covenant [...]

**3:2** [...] and from the dawn I seek You, and as certain as the daybreak You appear to me [...]

**3:3** [...] You have opened my ears to the discipline of those who reprove in righteousness [...]

**3:4** [...] and the interpreters of knowledge [...] with servants of truth [...]

**3:5** [...] You have done this for Your glory [...] to declare Your power [...]

**3:6** [...] and how shall the spirit of flesh comprehend all these things [...]

**3:7** [...] and how shall he discern [...] the great purpose of Your [...]

**3:8** [...] and the dwelling of [...] the holy ones [...]

**3:9** [...] and the fountain of understanding [...] the wellspring of might [...]

**3:10** [...] and the glory of [...] concealed from the assembly of flesh [...]

**3:11** [...] I seek You and as certain as the dawn You appear to me [...]

**3:12** [...] and they, those who lead Your people astray, have come against me [...]

**3:13** [...] for they serve their inclination [...] and they have not sought You [...]

**3:14** [...] in that which You commanded [...] they chose what You abhor [...]

**3:15** [...] and they rejected what You love [...] for the obstinacy of their heart [...]

**3:16** [...] they have assembled against me [...] the members of my council [...]

**3:17** [...] and those who eat my bread have raised the heel against me [...]

**3:18** [...] and all who joined my fellowship have spoken treacherously against me [...]

**3:19** [...] and the men of my confidence [...] have turned to the interpreters of falsehood [...]

**3:20** [...] with a deceitful tongue [...] and with venomous speech they have spoken [...]

**3:21** [...] interpreters of error and seers of deception have schemed against me [...]

**3:22** [...] and they have exchanged Your Law within my heart for flattery toward Your people [...]

**3:23** [...] and they withhold the drink of knowledge from the thirsty [...]

**3:24** [...] and for their thirst they offer them vinegar to drink [...]

**3:25** [...] that they might gaze upon their error and become frenzied at their festivals [...]

**3:26** [...] and be caught in their nets [...]

**3:27** [...] but You, O God, despise every scheme of Belial [...]

**3:28** [...] and it is Your counsel that shall stand [...]

**3:29** [...] and the purpose of Your heart that endures forever [...]

**3:30** [...] and they, the dissemblers, devise schemes of Belial [...]

**3:31** [...] they seek You with a divided heart [...] and are not established in Your truth [...]

**3:32** [...] a root that yields poison and wormwood is in their designs [...]

**3:33** [...] and in the obstinacy of their heart they go astray [...]

**3:34** [...] and they seek You among idols [...]

**3:35** [...] and the stumbling-block of their guilt they have placed before their faces [...]

**3:36** [...] and they come to inquire of You [...] from the mouth of lying prophets led astray by error [...]

**3:37** [...] and they speak with an alien tongue to Your people [...] and with a strange speech [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 3 preserves a hymn of the persecuted teacher figure. "Made my face to shine" (3:1) echoes the Aaronic blessing of Numbers 6:25. The vinegar-for-knowledge image (3:24) foreshadows Gospel passion accounts. "Root producing poison and wormwood" (3:32) alludes to Deuteronomy 29:18. The "double heart" (lev va-lev, 3:31) is a biblical idiom for duplicity (cf. Psalm 12:2).*
